TRAINER_LEAF_ALTERING_CAVE.assessment: Ninetales and Scrappy Kangaskhan establish a recognizably Kanto opening; Gengar/Tangrowth continue that identity, with Zeraora and Mega Mewtwo Y adding exceptional power. Preserve the broad Kanto ensemble rather than invent a single mandatory starter for Leaf.
TRAINER_LEAF_ALTERING_CAVE.lead_and_reserve_ai: Mega Mewtwo Y's actual ability and changed defenses affect targeting; Chlorophyll and powders require actual sun and valid targets. Do not treat Zeraora's Plasma Fists as harmless to same-turn Normal attack plans.
TRAINER_LEAF_ALTERING_CAVE.counterplay_review: Ground/Water pressures Ninetales subject to sun, Fighting threatens Kangaskhan and Ghost/Dark pressures Gengar/Mewtwo. Powder immunity challenges Tangrowth; account for Plasma Fists changing eligible Normal move interactions in its turn.
TRAINER_LEAF_ALTERING_CAVE.final_plan: Leaf, Kanto's Champion, in the Altering Cave: Drought Ninetales, Scrappy Kangaskhan's Fake Out, Cursed Body Gengar's Icy Wind, Chlorophyll Tangrowth's Sleep Powder and Rage Powder, Zeraora's Plasma Fists, and Mega Mewtwo Y's Psystrike.
shared_ai_dependencies: Mega Mewtwo Y's actual ability and changed defenses affect targeting; Chlorophyll and powders require actual sun and valid targets. Do not treat Zeraora's Plasma Fists as harmless to same-turn Normal attack plans.

baseline.plan: Steven's steel and stone: Sturdy Skarmory's Tailwind and Body Press, the Rayquaza he met atop Sky Pillar Dragon Dances into Dragon Ascent, Storm Drain Cradily's Stealth Rock, Iron Fist Melmetal's Double Iron Bash behind a Weakness Policy, Dialga's Draco Meteor, and Mega Metagross's Tough Claws Meteor Mash.
baseline.counterplay: Fire hits Skarmory, Melmetal, Dialga and Metagross, Fighting hits Cradily, Melmetal and Dialga, Ice quadruples on Rayquaza and Fairy hits it, Ground hits Metagross, Melmetal and Dialga, and hitting Melmetal super effectively triggers its Policy.

TRAINER_STEVEN.assessment: Skarmory, Cradily and Metagross already give Steven a substantial iconic core. Rayquaza, Melmetal and Dialga strengthen it without replacing the identity. Preserve all loadouts, but explicitly allocate the shared Mega budget: Dragon Ascent makes Rayquaza a second eligible candidate despite its Sash, so Metagross's planned Mega cannot be assumed.
TRAINER_STEVEN.lead_and_reserve_ai: Shared Mega allocation must compare Rayquaza's move-enabled transformation with Metagross's stone and keep one actual activation per trainer. Default the planned Metagross finish unless a verified stronger immediate Rayquaza line justifies spending the budget; evaluate Policy only after Melmetal survives.
TRAINER_STEVEN.counterplay_review: Fire pressures Skarmory/Melmetal/Metagross but is neutral on Steel/Dragon Dialga. Ground/Fighting threatens the Steel core and Ice strongly pressures Rayquaza. Strong super-effective damage can KO Melmetal before Policy helps; inspect which Pokémon actually receives the Mega budget.
TRAINER_STEVEN.final_plan: Skarmory supports Rayquaza with Tailwind, while Cradily supplies Storm Drain and recovery, Melmetal threatens Policy-enhanced physical damage and Dialga supplies special coverage. Mega Metagross is the signature planned finish. Dragon Ascent also makes Rayquaza Mega-eligible; one shared Mega activation is allocated by the common AI, favoring Metagross on equivalent lines rather than forbidding a necessary winning Rayquaza transformation.

baseline.plan: Natural Cure Roserade threatens sleep and Leaf Storm beside Togekiss's redirection and paralysis. Spiritomb weakens opposing offense, Scarf Lucario covers both defenses, and Specs Miraidon controls the late terrain phase. Mega Garchomp Z uses partner-safe Ground coverage beside these grounded allies.
baseline.counterplay: Fire and Ice hit Roserade, Rock and Electric hit Togekiss, Fairy hits Spiritomb and Garchomp, Fire, Fighting and Ground hit Lucario, Ice, Ground, Dragon and Fairy hit Miraidon, Ice quadruples on Garchomp, and Miraidon is locked into one move.

TRAINER_CYNTHIA_1.assessment: Roserade/Togekiss establish sleep and redirection, with Spiritomb control and Lucario mixed coverage before Miraidon and Mega Garchomp Z. Garchomp, Spiritomb, Roserade, Togekiss and Lucario preserve Cynthia's iconic ensemble. The late Electric Terrain phase is intentional and should not invalidate the opening sleep plan prematurely.
TRAINER_CYNTHIA_1.lead_and_reserve_ai: Mega Garchomp Z is pure Dragon in the configured data, losing Ground STAB and four-times Ice weakness. Schedule Miraidon after sleep has served its purpose or when Electric Terrain's offensive value outweighs it; use actual form ability slots.
TRAINER_CYNTHIA_1.counterplay_review: Fire/Ice pressures Roserade, Rock/Electric threatens Togekiss and Fairy pressures Spiritomb/Garchomp. Ground/Ice/Dragon/Fairy threatens Miraidon. Mega Garchomp Z is only twice weak to Ice and has no Ground typing; exploit Scarf/Specs locking with the actual terrain state.
TRAINER_CYNTHIA_1.final_plan: Roserade/Togekiss establish sleep and redirection, with Spiritomb control and Lucario mixed coverage before Miraidon and Mega Garchomp Z.
